claim: GRAMMAR 3 teaches that the present form of a verb expresses a habitual action when used with frequency words such as まいにち, and no card in either unit explains this.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "The present form of verbs also expresses habitual actions when they are used with adverbs of frequency or words used with every time, such as まいにち (every day), まいしゅう (every week), and まいあさ (every morning)." KS3 スミスさんは まいにち コーヒーを のみます is carded (ks3-drinks-coffee) with no note; the まいにち, まいあさ, まいばん, まいしゅう cards only explain the まい prefix. No note in chapter-9 or chapter-9-extras mentions habitual meaning.
fix: Add a note to ks3-drinks-coffee (or mainichi-everyday) saying the ます form with まいにち and the other frequency words describes something done regularly, not only a future action.

claim: Exercise I tells the learner to memorise present and past, affirmative and negative forms of five verbs, and 9 of the 20 cells have no card.
evidence: Book, EXERCISE I: "Repeat the verbs below and memorize their forms" with a table of でんわを します/しません/しました/しませんでした, おくります/おくりません/おくりました/おくりませんでした, あいます/あいません/あいました/あいませんでした, ききます..., おしえます/おしえません/おしえました/おしえませんでした. Carded: でんわをします, おくります, おくりました (v9-haha-ni-meru), あいます, あいました (ex9-senshu-wa-koko-de-aimashita), all four きき- forms (Lesson 8 and ask-phone-number), おしえます, おしえました (ks2-told-location). No card in the collection through Lesson 9 holds でんわをしません, でんわをしました, でんわをしませんでした, おくりません, おくりませんでした, あいません, あいませんでした, おしえません or おしえませんでした (bare しません/しました/しませんでした exist in chapter-8). Lesson 8 covered all 28 of its table cells with a form set in the extras.
fix: Add a form set in chapter-9-extras like Lesson 8's, one fixed sentence per verb cycled through the four forms, so each missing cell has a card.

claim: The book lists いい (nice, good) as this lesson's vocabulary and prints いい みせですね in the dialogue, but both cards are excluded as premature on the grounds that Lesson 10 teaches いい.
evidence: Book, Target Dialogue VOCABULARY: "いい nice, good"; dialogue line スミス: いい みせですね。 Card ii-nice excluded, reviewNote: "Possibly premature — explicitly taught later in Lesson 10". Card ex9-ii-mise-desu-ne (chapter-9-extras) excluded for the same reason. Lesson 8 already cards いいですね, and chapter-10 cards いい, so the gap lasts one lesson.
fix: Restore ii-nice and ex9-ii-mise-desu-ne, since the book introduces the word here; the Lesson 10 card can then build on it.

claim: The note says the sentence stacks three に with different jobs, but it has two.
evidence: Card target: スミスさんはげつようびの４じにとうきょうえきですずきさんにあいます. Note: "person は — day/time に — place で — target に — verb, stacking three に's with different jobs in one sentence." The only に are after ４じ (time) and すずきさん (target); とうきょうえき takes で.
fix: Change "stacking three に's" to "two に with different jobs: time and the person met".

claim: The note calls the two words for "my wife" (or "my husband") two readings of the same word, but they are different words the book lists as alternatives.
evidence: Book, WORD POWER: "つま ／ かない (my) wife" and "おっと ／ しゅじん (my) husband", a slash between two separate words. Card note: "Also read かない (kanai) — both mean 'my wife'". The deck's own kanai-wife and shujin-husband cards explain them as distinct words ("literally 'inside the house'", "literally 'master'").
fix: Reword to "another word for my wife (or husband)" and drop "reading" and "same word".

claim: The note says あいます takes に and "not と", which the book does not say and which reads as if と were wrong with あいます.
evidence: Card note: "Takes に (ni) for the person met, as in たなかさんにあいます — not と (to, 'with') from Lesson 6, which marks doing something together." Book GRAMMAR 1 only says に marks the person the action is directed at; it makes no claim about と. たなかさんとあいます (meeting by mutual arrangement) is also normal Japanese.
fix: Keep "takes に for the person met" and drop the "not と" clause, or say that this lesson uses に.

claim: The English says Smith asked Nakamura-san for "his" phone number, but the book draws Nakamura-san as a woman.
evidence: Card English: "Smith-san asked Nakamura-san for his phone number." Book, EXERCISE III picture e.g. 1 labels なかむらさん under a woman with earrings; EXERCISE IV pictures show the same woman answering, with the address "mayumi_n@".
fix: Change "his" to "her".

claim: The English says Nakamura-san told Smith-san "his" phone number; Nakamura-san is a woman in the book, and "his" also reads as Smith's own number.
evidence: Card English: "Nakamura-san told Smith-san his phone number." Book, EXERCISE IV: the woman in the pictures (なかむらさん, "mayumi_n@") gives her number to Smith.
fix: Change "his" to "her".

claim: The note places the ええ reply in conversation "with restaurant staff you know", but in the book Suzuki gives it to his colleague Smith.
evidence: Card note: "ええ (ē) is a softer, more casual 'yes' than はい (hai) — natural in relaxed conversation with restaurant staff you know." Book, Target Dialogue: スミス: すずきさんは よく この みせに きますか。 すずき: ええ、ときどき きます。
fix: Change the note to "natural in relaxed conversation, as with a colleague".

claim: The card asks the learner to produce おきます (get up), which no card teaches before Lesson 21.
evidence: Card target: まいにち、なんじにおきますか, "What time do you get up every day?" The Lesson 9 chapter does not use おきます; the first おきます vocabulary card in the collection is in chapter-21. No earlier unit has it.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 21's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: The card asks the learner to produce おきます (get up), which no card teaches before Lesson 21.
evidence: Card target: わたしは、はちじにおきます, "I get up at eight o'clock." The first おきます vocabulary card in the collection is in chapter-21; Lesson 9 does not use the verb.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 21's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: The card asks the learner to produce ねました (went to bed), and ねます is first taught in Lesson 17.
evidence: Card target: じゅうにじにねました, "I went to bed at twelve." The first ねます card in the collection is in chapter-17; Lesson 9 does not use the verb.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 17's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: The card uses ねます (first taught in Lesson 17) and さくばん (last night), which no card in the collection teaches.
evidence: Card target: さくばん、なんじにねましたか, "What time did you go to bed last night?" Neither word is in this chapter; ねます is first carded in chapter-17 and no unit has a さくばん card. The note supplies the meaning of さくばん, but the verb is untaught.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 17's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: The card is built on どう (how), which this chapter does not teach and which its own note says is introduced in Lesson 11.
evidence: Card target: にほんはどうですか, "How do you like Japan?" Note: "The word is formally introduced in Lesson 11." reviewNote: "Form coverage for どうですか, taught in this lesson", but Lesson 9 never uses どう; the only earlier どう- cards are どうぞ, どうも and どうやって.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 11's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: The card is built on どうでしたか, which the book teaches in Lesson 11, not here.
evidence: Card target: りょこうはどうでしたか, "How was the trip?" Lesson 9 never uses どう; the companion card f9-nihon-wa-do-desu-ka says "The word is formally introduced in Lesson 11", and that card's note names どうでしたか as a Lesson 11 form.
fix: Move the card to Lesson 11's extras, or exclude it here.

claim: An authored card teaches the book's invented restaurant name レストランローマ as part of the answer.
evidence: Book, EXERCISE V VOCABULARY: "レストランローマ Restaurant Rome (fictitious restaurant name)". Card (aiSuggested): レストランローマのばしょをおしえてください, "Please tell me the location of Restaurant Rome." reviewNote: "Vocabulary coverage for レストランローマ".
fix: Exclude the card, or rebuild it on a common noun the learner knows, for example かいぎのばしょ or レストランのばしょ.

claim: The card teaches the book's fictitious library name しぶやとしょかん as part of the answer.
evidence: Book, EXERCISE IX VOCABULARY: "しぶやとしょかん Shibuya Library (fictitious library name)". Card: しぶやとしょかんにいきます, "I will go to the Shibuya Library."
fix: Keep the book line if wanted, but consider としょかん alone, which the learner has from Lesson 8.

claim: The card teaches the book's fictitious library name しぶやとしょかん as part of the answer.
evidence: Book, EXERCISE IX VOCABULARY: "しぶやとしょかん Shibuya Library (fictitious library name)". Card: エマさんはよくしぶやとしょかんにいきますか, "Do you often go to the Shibuya Library, Emma-san?"
fix: Consider としょかん alone, as the f9-*-toshokan cards in the extras already do.

claim: The note explains こども by pointing to こ, おんなのこ and おとこのこ "from Lesson 13", words the learner meets four lessons later.
evidence: Card note: "こ (ko, 'child') from Lesson 13 is the shorter root that builds おんなのこ (onna no ko, 'girl') and おとこのこ (otoko no ko, 'boy')." None of the three is carded before Lesson 9.
fix: Drop the Lesson 13 sentence from the note, or move it to the Lesson 13 こ card.

claim: The card ships, but its reviewNote says the semantic de-dup pass excluded it, so one of the two is wrong.
evidence: reviewNote: "Excluded by the semantic de-dup pass. Pattern: [person] に (メールを) おくります. The source already drills this frame repeatedly ... so another noun-swap adds nothing." The card has no excluded flag in cards.json or corpus.json, and qa-render-unit lists it among the 98 shipping cards.
fix: Either set excluded as the reviewNote says, or update the reviewNote to record why it was restored.
